lead: Very old writings, like clay tablets from Babylon, Chinese court diaries and Sanskrit verses, still hold clues for scientists today. This page opens four “case files”, tests each old claim with modern science, and gives an honest verdict.
try: Start with Case 1, “Did the planets really gather at the start of the Kali Yuga?” (an age that Indian texts say began in 3102 BC). Read where the planets sat that night, then drag the Days from the Kali Yuga epoch slider away from zero and watch them spread out.
points: An old Indian text says all the planets lined up when the Kali Yuga began. The real sky shows a loose group, not one exact point, so the verdict is “partly true”.
Eclipses written down long ago show that the Earth’s spin is slowly getting slower, because the Moon’s tides act like a brake.
Chinese astronomers saw a “guest star” in the year 1054. Today the leftover cloud from that exploding star is called the Crab Nebula.
